tagline.en: A fast world-action model for robot policies, built on Wan with a Mixture-of-Transformers action graph.
tagline.zh: 一个面向机器人策略的快速世界-动作模型，基于 Wan、采用 Mixture-of-Transformers 动作图。

en: FastWAM is a world-action model (WAM) for robot manipulation. It takes camera views and robot state and predicts an action chunk, using a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) action-inference graph paired with a Wan VAE and a UMT5 text encoder.

It comes with official checkpoints for two popular manipulation settings — LIBERO and RoboTwin — each with matching normalization statistics. The MoT policy is roughly 12 GB before the VAE and text encoder load; instruction embeddings are cached (the UMT5 encoder defaults to CPU, and you can supply precomputed 4096-dimensional tokens), and the video expert's key/value tensors are prefetched once and reused across denoising steps to keep inference fast.
In WorldFoundry you stage a checkpoint locally, pick the LIBERO or RoboTwin variant with its official camera/state contract, and it returns a finite action chunk for the robot.
zh: FastWAM 是一个面向机器人操作的世界-动作模型（WAM）。它接收相机视角与机器人状态并预测一段动作，采用 Mixture-of-Transformers（MoT）动作推理图，搭配 Wan VAE 与 UMT5 文本编码器。
它附带针对两个常用操作场景的官方 checkpoint——LIBERO 与 RoboTwin——各自带有配套的归一化统计。MoT 策略在加载 VAE 与文本编码器前约为 12 GB；指令嵌入会被缓存（UMT5 编码器默认放在 CPU，你也可以直接提供预先算好的 4096 维 token），而视频专家的 key/value 张量只预取一次并在各去噪步之间复用，从而保持推理快速。
在 WorldFoundry 中，你把 checkpoint 放到本地，按官方相机/状态约定选择 LIBERO 或 RoboTwin 变体，它便返回给机器人的一段动作。

whenToUse.en: Use it when you want a Wan-based world-action policy for robot manipulation with ready checkpoints for LIBERO and RoboTwin, and an inference path tuned for speed.
whenToUse.zh: 当你想要一个基于 Wan 的世界-动作策略用于机器人操作，并希望有 LIBERO 与 RoboTwin 的现成 checkpoint、以及为速度调优的推理路径时使用。

notFor.en: Its output is an action chunk for robot control, not general video. Checkpoints and their statistics are staged locally, so plan for the download and disk space.
notFor.zh: 它的输出是用于机器人控制的动作，而非通用视频。Checkpoint 及其统计需放到本地，请预留下载时间与磁盘空间。

en: World-action policy on a Mixture-of-Transformers action graph

MoT policy is roughly 12 GB before VAE and text encoder load
Cached instruction embeddings and prefetched key/value tensors speed up inference
